newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INSIGHT-Australian bonds off new lows, damage done.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INSIGHT-Australian bonds off new lows, damage done.

text.p: *Australian bond futures ended above new lows for the year set in SYCOM, but with key support levels broken during Monday's dayside session the outlook remains extremely bearish.

Australian bond futures contracts ended above new lows for the year struck in afterhours trading, but with key support levels broken during Monday's dayside session the outlook remains extremely bearish.
The March 10-year bond futures contract ended SYCOM at 92.170, just a tad above Monday's 92.165 pit close, but not before it had tumbled to 92.090.

Heavy offshore selling on Monday saw the contract cut through a cluster of support levels around 92.210, and while 92.090 has provided a solid bounce, a breakdown here would open the way to the psychological 92.000 and the 91.950.
The 91.950 level represents a 50-percent retracement of the June to December 1997 rally from 90.920 to 93.015.

However, analysts view the current sell-off in domestic debt markets as overdone, particularly at the short end where December bill futures are indicating a monetary policy tightening of over 75 basis points by the end of the year.

The 10-year bond contract is also signalling an oversold position with its relative strength index currently around 25 percent, and March three-year bonds and near-term bills futures contracts are not far behind.

The market faces a severe test with January retail trade and building approvals due at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), which are seen as equally as important as Wednesday's fourth quarter GDP as they will give an indication of consumer spending this year.

The retail sector is expected to have rebounded after a subdued fourth quarter and economists' median forecasts centre on a 1.5 percent rise after the 1.0 percent fall in December, according to a Reuters survey.
Building approvals are expected to show continuing signs of improvement amid a general strengthening in the economy. Forecasts here centre on a 2.0 percent increase.
